text: Aircraft Operators covered under this program must submit information for all passengers to Secure Flight in the form of SFPD.  The vast majority of SFPD messages submitted by the Aircraft Operators are identified as a low or neutral risk by the Secure Fight automated engine.  Those records identified as requiring additional review are inhibited by the Secure Flight engine, and the passengers with inhibited boarding pass must go the Aircraft Operator ticket counter for additional assistance.  Aircraft Operators must submit additional information on inhibited passengers to TSA.  Generally, this information is gathered from the passenger’s VID and submitted electronically to TSA (a VID submission).  There are currently 222 Aircraft Operators covered by this collection; in addition, TSA expects 20 Aircraft Operators per year to be added each year.  TSA estimates an average of 990 annual VID submissions per covered Aircraft Operator, and 130 seconds (0.0361 hours) per response.  Certain submissions may require a Resolution Call to TSA to provide additional information.  TSA estimates that each carrier will be required to make an average of 230 calls per year.  TSA estimates a Resolution Call will require 12 minutes (0.2 hours).  The total annual hour burden for covered Aircraft Operators is 21,418.5 hours, or 64,256 hours over 3 years.  Table 1 summarizes these estimates.

text: The mean hourly wage rate for reservation and transportation ticket agents is $23.77. The fully loaded wage rate is calculated by multiplying the mean hourly wage of reservation and transportation ticket agents ($23.77) by a compensation factor. text: Aircraft Operators covered under this program must submit information for all passengers to Secure Flight in the form of SFPD.  The vast majority of SFPD messages submitted by the Aircraft Operators are identified as a low or neutral risk by the Secure Fight automated engine.  Those records identified as requiring additional review are inhibited by the Secure Flight engine, and the passengers with inhibited boarding pass must go the Aircraft Operator ticket counter for additional assistance.  Aircraft Operators must submit additional information on inhibited passengers to TSA.  Generally, this information is gathered from the passenger’s verifying identity document (VID) and submitted electronically to TSA (a VID submission).  There are currently 211 Aircraft Operators covered by this collection; in addition, TSA expects 20 Aircraft Operators per year to be added each year.  TSA estimates an average of 865 annual VID submissions per covered Aircraft Operator, and 130 seconds (0.0361 hours) per response.  Certain submissions may require a Resolution Call to TSA to provide additional information.  TSA estimates that each carrier will be required to make an average of 149 calls per year.  TSA estimates a Resolution Call will require 5 minutes and 10 seconds (0.0862 hours).  The total annual hour burden for covered Aircraft Operators is 10,178.39 hours, or 30,535 hours over 3 years.  Table 1 summarizes these estimates.

text: TSA estimates the total cost to the Federal government associated with the EXIS® ICR to be approximately $886,729 annually.  This includes TSA staff costs and other infrastructure costs to maintain and update EXIS®.  TSA staff costs were calculated by assuming a H/I band program analyst receiving an annual H/I band blended fully-loaded compensation of $167,819.  Program analysts will each spend roughly 20 hours per week on EXIS®-related duties.  This estimate was used to calculate a TSA full-time employee (FTE) of 1.5 (3 employees multiplied by 20 hours per week multiplied by 52 weeks (3,020) then divided by 2,087 hours.  TSA multiplies $167,819 by 1.5 FTE to estimate a program analyst cost of $251,729.  In addition, TSA estimates the annual contracting cost to be $635,000.00 based on an existing EXIS® contract.  The total annual cost to the Federal government is $251,729 + $635,000 = $886,729, or $2,660,187 over 3 years.  See Table 7.

text: TSA calculated the weighted average wage rate of $67.87 for the hourly burden for managers in multiple transportation modes based on past participation per mode and the average hourly wage rate for managers.  TSA used the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) Occupational Employment Statistics (OES) data on Standard Occupation Code (SOC) 11-1021 General and Operations Managers for each transportation mode that has participated in EXIS®. Aviation had 403 participants, NAICS 481000 - Air Transportation had an average hourly wage rate of $74.47), Maritime had 33 participants (NAICS 483000 Water Transportation had an average hourly wage rate of $73.58), Highway and Motor Carrier had 66 participants (485200 Interurban and Rural Bus Transportation had average hourly wages of $58.24), Mass Transit and Passenger Railroads had 165 participants (NAICS 485100 Urban Transit Transportation had an average hourly wage rate of $48.08), Pipeline had 34 participants (NAICS 486000 Pipeline Transportation had an average hourly wage rate of $80.48), Postal and Shipping had three participants (NAICS 491000 Postal Service Transportation had an average hourly wage rate of $76.17), Freight Railroads had 154 participants (NAICS 482000 - Rail Transportation had an average hourly wage rate of $71.75).  TSA then accounts for compensation and benefits with a compensation factor of 1.45314, calculated by total compensation of $46.21 divided by wages of $31.80 for All Civilian Workers.  TSA multiplies the weighted average hourly wage rate $67.87 by 1.45314 to calculate a loaded wage rate of $98.62.  Sources: BLS, OES, SOC, https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/May/naics3_481000.htm https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/May/naics3_483000.htm
